fuel-injector-1.summary: Injector 1 meters fuel at its intake port. Its two electrical contacts share the relay supply and a PCM driver with two other injectors.

steps.title: Supply the coil
steps.text: C190 receives circuit361 R through the shared S158 supply branch.

steps.title: Recognize the shared driver
steps.text: Circuit555 T connects this injector and cylinders 1, 3 and 5 to C185/58. The odd group uses S160/C101/12; the even group uses S159/C101/13. Both pass through C125. This grouping establishes connections, not injection timing or firing order.

steps.title: Keep terminals unassigned
steps.text: The modeled terminal1/terminal2 names are CAD identities. The reviewed diagram does not number the component cavities.

troubleshooting.title: Reason from the circuit
troubleshooting.text: A concern shared by the three injectors in one group makes the common driver path relevant; a concern spanning both groups also makes shared361 supply relevant. This is circuit-based reasoning, not a diagnosis that the PCM or a splice has failed.

fuel-injector-1.limits: 1994 4.9L EVTM connection evidence; actual calibration and harness condition unknown. iac-valve-body.summary: The IAC valve changes bypass air under PCM control to regulate idle.

steps.title: Identify the two electrical paths
steps.text: C1007 has361 R relay supply and264 W/LB control through C101/4 to PCM C185/21. The EVTM describes a duty-cycle command.

steps.title: Follow the air function
steps.text: The solenoid acts on the air-control valve. The electrical map does not calibrate the illustrated spring, valve travel or airflow.

troubleshooting.title: Reason from the circuit
troubleshooting.text: The command circuit and shared supply are distinct possible electrical paths to inspect in the applicable diagnostic procedure. An idle symptom alone does not distinguish wiring from an air-path or valve problem.

egr-vacuum-regulator.summary: EVR is the electrical actuator that regulates vacuum supplied to the EGR valve; EVP is the separate position feedback sensor.

steps.title: Follow the command
steps.text: C180 connects361 R supply and360 BR/PK through C101/3 to PCM C185/33. The source PCM table calls this Input while the schematic shows a solenoid connection; no waveform is inferred.

steps.title: Follow the feedback separately
steps.text: The EVP reports EGR valve position through352 BR/LG to PCM27; it is a separate three-contact interface.

troubleshooting.title: Reason from the circuit
troubleshooting.text: A commanded vacuum path and a position-feedback path are different parts of the system. Comparing those paths is useful reasoning; the EVTM does not supply a vacuum threshold or prove the illustrated internal mechanism is the installed revision.

egr-position-sensor.summary: EVP reports EGR valve position to the PCM using reference, signal and sensor-return connections.

steps.title: Separate reference, signal and return
steps.text: C182 uses351 BR/W at PCM26,352 BR/LG at PCM27, and359 GY/R at PCM46. C101 cavities are38,27 and39 respectively.

steps.title: Distinguish sensor return
steps.text: 359 is the sensor signal return shared with TPS and temperature sensing. It is not the oxygen-sensor89 ground or heater/chassis57 ground.

troubleshooting.title: Reason from the circuit
troubleshooting.text: Because the reference and return are shared, related sensor concerns can involve a shared circuit as well as an individual sensor. This relationship does not establish the cause or justify grounding a sensor-return wire to the chassis.

throttle-sensor.summary: TPS converts throttle position into a PCM input using a reference-fed resistive sensor.

steps.title: Follow the three circuits
steps.text: C1026 uses351 BR/W reference at PCM26,355 GY/W signal at PCM47 and359 GY/R sensor return at PCM46; C101 cavities38,37 and39.

steps.title: Keep related interfaces separate
steps.text: MAP uses the same reference and return families but its own358 LG/BK signal to PCM45. MAP geometry is absent from this inventory; this is connection context, not a selectable part.

troubleshooting.title: Reason from the circuit
troubleshooting.text: Shared reference/return paths are relevant when several related inputs disagree. The source provides no calibrated TPS voltage range or adjustment procedure here.

engine-coolant-temperature-assembly.summary: The two-lead ECT reports coolant temperature to the PCM. Its thermistor resistance decreases as temperature rises.

steps.title: Trace the temperature input
steps.text: C183 connects354 LG/R through C125 and C101/5 to PCM7;359 GY/R returns through S138/C125/S161/C101/39/S137 to PCM46.

steps.title: Recognize the intake-temperature partner
steps.text: IAT C164 shares359 return and sends743 GY through C125/C101/6 to PCM25. ACT/IAT names do not establish two separate devices. IAT geometry is absent here.

steps.title: Separate oxygen and heater grounds
steps.text: The unmodeled HO2S C1025 has74 GY/LB signal to PCM29 and89 O oxygen ground to PCM49, plus298 P/O heater supply and57 BK heater/chassis ground viaG101. All four pass through inline C1003; it is not a second sensor. None is a replacement for359 sensor return.

troubleshooting.title: Reason from the circuit
troubleshooting.text: ECT and IAT share a return, so that connection is relevant to a concern affecting both. Oxygen sensing and its heater have different return paths. No resistance curve, temperature calibration or live test procedure is supplied by this map.
